lead.heading: I measure my leadership by what my team can do without me.
lead.intro: The products matter, but the lasting result is people who can run a domain on their own — and an organization that decides from customer evidence.
lead.habit_1.title: Customer evidence over internal opinion
lead.habit_1.body: Brought direct user discovery to a product org that had none — 50+ agent conversations at eXp, 200+ customer interviews at Virbela.
lead.habit_2.title: Teams that own outcomes
lead.habit_2.body: Organize around accountable business domains instead of a central review queue — PMs and engineering partners own the result together.
lead.habit_3.title: Technical enough to be useful
lead.habit_3.body: SQL, APIs, auth and data semantics with engineering — close enough to the system to make good tradeoffs, clear about who owns the architecture.
lead.coaching.heading: How I grow product managers
lead.coaching.intro: The path I used to take four business analysts to independent product managers — and to coach PMs through Senior PM.
lead.coaching.step_1.title: Give them a domain, not a backlog
lead.coaching.step_1.body: Restructure ownership around a real business area, so each person is accountable for outcomes — not just tickets.
lead.coaching.step_2.title: Teach discovery, not feature intake
lead.coaching.step_2.body: Probe past the requested feature to the underlying workflow, validate with users, and bring that evidence into prioritization.
lead.coaching.step_3.title: Clear the busywork
lead.coaching.step_3.body: Roll out AI-assisted workflows for story writing — ~20 PMs and partners trained — and reinvest the time in customers and stakeholders.
lead.coaching.step_4.title: Hand over the roadmap
lead.coaching.step_4.body: They own discovery, stakeholder relationships, prioritization and delivery for their domain. I move to coach and unblock.
